We need to propose a retrosynthesis route (max 3 steps) to target molecule: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We need leaves commercially available, total price <= $9999. Need to find suitable disconnections.

The molecule has a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to a phenyl ring bearing a sulfonyl group attached to another phenyl ring with a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide (cinnamamide) attached to an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). Actually structure: p-tolyl-sulfonyl attached to phenyl which is para-substituted with the sulfonyl group linking to another phenyl bearing a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (para-aminophenyl). Wait: Let's parse: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

So tolyl (methyl phenyl) attached via sulfonamide to phenyl (c2) which is para-substituted with a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). So overall: p-tolyl-sulfonyl-para-phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-aniline.

Potential retrosynthetic disconnections:

1) Disconnection of sulfonamide: break S-N bond to give sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonic acid) and aniline (p-toluidine). So we could have p-toluidine (commercial) reacting with sulfonyl chloride derived from 4-(cinnamoyl)aniline phenyl sulfonyl chloride? Actually the sulfonyl part is attached to phenyl ring (c2) which also bears the cinnamoyl anilide substituent. So we could think of forming the sulfonamide by reacting p-toluidine with 4-(cinnamoyl)aniline phenyl sulfonyl chloride (i.e., 4-(cinnamoyl)aniline phenyl sulfonyl chloride). That sulfonyl chloride could be made from the corresponding sulfonic acid (by chlorination) or from sulfonylation of the phenyl ring using SO2Cl2? But maybe easier: start from 4-(cinnamoyl)aniline phenyl sulfonyl chloride is not common.

Alternative: Disconnection at the amide bond: break C(=O)-NH to give aniline (c3) and cinnamic acid derivative (trans-3-phenylacrylic acid attached to phenyl). So we could have 4-aminobenzoyl (aniline) reacting with trans-cinnamic acid (or its activated form). Actually the amide is between the cinnamoyl carbonyl and an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). So we could form the amide by coupling 4-aminobenzoyl (p-aminobenzoyl?) Wait the amide carbonyl is attached to the phenyl ring (c2) via the double bond: /C=C/C(=O)N-... So the carbonyl is attached to the phenyl ring via the double bond (cinnamoyl). So the amide is between the cinnamoyl carbonyl and an aniline (p-aminophenyl). So we could get the cinnamoyl acid (trans-4-(sulfonyl phenyl)cinnamic acid) and couple with p-phenylenediamine? Actually the amide nitrogen is attached to an aniline (c3ccccc3N) which is an aniline (para-? Actually it's just an aniline with an NH2 at para? The SMILES: Nc3ccccc3N indicates an aniline with an NH attached to carbonyl and also an NH2 at para? Wait "Nc3ccccc3N" means an aniline where the nitrogen attached to carbonyl is attached to the aromatic carbon (position 1) and there is another N attached to the aromatic carbon at position? Actually "Nc3ccccc3N" is an aniline with an NH attached to the aromatic carbon (the first N) and also an NH2 substituent at the other end? The SMILES: N c3 c c c c c3 N. That is an aniline with an amino group at the opposite position? The first N is attached to the aromatic carbon (position 1) as substituent; the second N is attached to the aromatic carbon as substituent (position 6). So it's p-phenylenediamine (1,4-diaminobenzene) but one of the amines is acylated (forming amide). So the product is N-(4-aminophenyl)-cinnamamide? Actually the amide nitrogen is attached to the aromatic carbon (position 1) of a phenyl ring that also has an NH2 at para (position 4). So the product is N-(4-aminophenyl)trans-cinnamamide.

Thus we could start from p-phenylenediamine (commercial) and trans-cinnamic acid (commercial) to form the amide via coupling (e.g., using EDC/HOBt). That yields N-(4-aminophenyl)cinnamamide (with free para NH2). Then we need to sulfonylate the para position of that phenyl (the one bearing the amide) with sulfonyl chloride derived from p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride? Actually the sulfonyl group attaches to the phenyl ring (c2) at para position relative to the cinnamoyl substituent. The sulfonyl group is attached to the phenyl ring via S(=O)(=O)- attached to the phenyl (c2) and then attached to the p-tolyl amine (forming sulfonamide). So we need to attach a sulfonyl chloride (p-tolylsulfonyl chloride) to the phenyl ring (c2) at para position (via electrophilic aromatic substitution? Actually sulfonylation of aromatic ring is via sulfonyl chloride under Friedel-Crafts? Not typical. More common is sulfonamide formation: the sulfonyl chloride reacts with an amine to give sulfonamide. Here the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to p-tolyl (the N of p-toluidine). So the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the phenyl ring (c2) as sulfonyl group (Ar-SO2-). So we need to have the sulfonyl chloride derived from p-tolylsulfonyl chloride? Wait p-tolyl is attached to nitrogen, not to sulfonyl group. The sulfonyl group is attached to the phenyl ring (c2) and the nitrogen is attached to p-tolyl. So the sulfonyl chloride would be 4-(p-tolylsulfonyl)chloride? Actually the sulfonyl chloride is Ar-SO2-Cl where Ar is the phenyl ring (c2). Then reacting with p-toluidine gives the sulfonamide. So we need 4-(sulfonyl chloride) phenyl with the cinnamoyl substituent already present. So we could first prepare the phenyl sulfonyl chloride (para-chlorosulfonyl) with the cinnamoyl substituent, then react with p-toluidine.

Thus retrosynthesis steps:

Step 1: Disconnection of sulfonamide: target -> sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2-Cl) + p-toluidine.

Step 2: Disconnection of amide: sulfonyl chloride precursor (Ar-SO2-Cl) derived from aromatic ring bearing cinnamoyl group. That aromatic precursor could be obtained by sulfonylation of 4-aminophenyl? Actually we need the sulfonyl chloride on the phenyl ring that also has the cinnamoyl substituent. So we could start from 4-aminophenyl (p-phenylenediamine) after amide formation we have N-(4-aminophenyl)cinnamamide (with free NH2). Then we could convert that free NH2 to sulfonyl chloride? No, we need sulfonyl chloride on the aromatic ring, not on nitrogen. So we need to introduce sulfonyl chloride onto the phenyl ring via chlorosulfonation (ClSO2Cl) of the aromatic ring (electrophilic substitution). That would give 4-(chlorosulfonyl)-cinnamoyl phenyl (Ar-SO2-Cl). Then react with p-toluidine to give sulfonamide.

Thus retrosynthesis:

Target (A) = p-tolyl-sulfonamide of phenyl-cinnamamide.

Disconnection 1: A -> p-toluidine (commercial) + B (4-(chlorosulfonyl)-cinnamoyl phenyl) (i.e., 4-(chlorosulfonyl)phenyl trans-cinnamamide). Reaction: sulfonamide formation.

Disconnection 2: B -> C (N-(4-aminophenyl)cinnamamide) + ClSO2Cl (chlorosulfonic acid) via electrophilic aromatic chlorosulfonation (introducing SO2Cl). Actually the transformation is chlorosulfonation of aromatic ring bearing the amide substituent. So B can be obtained from C by chlorosulfonation (ClSO3H). So step 2: C -> B via chlorosulfonation.

Disconnection 3: C (N-(4-aminophenyl)cinnamamide) can be formed by amide coupling of p-phenylenediamine (commercial) with trans-cinnamic acid (commercial). Reaction: amide bond formation.

Thus three steps total.

Now we need to verify commercial availability and price constraints. Likely p-toluidine, p-phenylenediamine, trans-cinnamic acid are commercially available and cheap (<$100 each). Chlorosulfonic acid is also cheap. So total cost well under $9999.

Now we need to produce JSON route with nodes: root molecule, children reaction nodes with template IDs. We need template IDs for each reaction. We need to search for templates matching these transformations.

We need to find a template for sulfonamide formation (reaction of sulfonyl chloride with amine). Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria with functional_groups_formed: ["sulfonamide"] maybe also bonds formed: "S-N". Let's try.
